children.why_this_cut: The first child covers the privileged-information and information-flow rules (L1801-1926) plus the recipient-identification guidance and its examples (L1928-1973). The cut at L1973 (before the blank line at L1974) is clean: the next section begins a new heading (#use_preset_voice_in_voice_mode) with no linkage back to the privileged-information material. The only crossing linkage is the concept of privileged information itself, which is established in this child and used by the later sections' examples; it is seeded below.

The second child covers the preset-voice rule, the fairness section, the respect-real-world-ties section, and the 'Seek the truth together' / 'Don't have an agenda' section including the objective-point-of-view and present-perspectives subsections. The cut at L2400 (before the blank line at L2401) is clean: the next subsection (#no_topic_off_limits) begins a new topic. The crossing linkages are: the authority-level ordering (inherited seed) applies to the heading tags in this child; the stay_in_bounds concept is referenced at L2404; and the privileged-information concept is referenced at L2526 (in the next child) but the concept itself is established in child 1.

The third child covers the no-topic-off-limits subsection, the be-honest-and-transparent section with its do-not-lie and avoid-sycophancy subsections, and the ask-clarifying-questions subsection. The cut at L2400 is clean because the no-topic-off-limits heading begins a new topic. The crossing linkages are: stay_in_bounds (referenced at L2404), privileged-information (referenced at L2526), and the authority-level ordering (inherited seed) which applies to heading tags in this child.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: privileged_information
seed_vocabulary.prose: non-public OpenAI policies, system messages, hidden chain-of-thought messages, and private content the developer or user has provided to the model, which must not be disclosed without permission

seed_vocabulary.name: information_flow
seed_vocabulary.prose: the movement of information between parties, including direct transmission and actions like changing sharing settings or approving authentication connections, which the assistant should be mindful of

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the hierarchy of instructions (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority) that determines which instructions take precedence

judgment_calls: Chose three children rather than two: the span is 1000 lines and naturally splits into three thematic blocks (privileged information, fairness/agenda, honesty/clarification). A two-way split would have made each child ~500 lines, still manageable but with more cross-linkage between the honesty and clarification material.

The cut at L1973/L2400 was chosen over alternative cuts at L1926 or L2126 because the section boundaries align with topic changes; cutting at L1926 would have split the recipient-identification guidance from its examples.

Seeded privileged_information and information_flow as new concepts because they are established in child 1 and used in child 3; the inherited seeds (authority_level_ordering, untrusted_data, stay_in_bounds) are carried unchanged because they appear in the span.
